responses.reason: R2 agrees the 0-100% axis leaves most of the rate plot empty but scores the choice 4 for being honest and consistently executed. I still score 3: the delivered primary chart is a nearly flat line at 97.4% with no change-from-baseline alternative, so the decisive comparison lives only in the insight band and KPI delta. A defensible anti-truncation rationale does not make the resulting chart decision-supportive.

R2 lowers this dimension because the order view is a 20-row sample without search or pagination. That limitation is real but I already priced it into ux_reasoning (3); the interaction itself is implemented — all states, a true-zero empty result, status focus and a scoped dialog with context chips. Counting the same sampling limit again here would double-penalise it, and no listed state is only described.

R2 scores Candidate B 2 for three contrast and three label/name mismatches, but that is the same finding set I already had, and B has no meaningful page overflow (392 vs 390) against Candidate A's 580px document, which I scored 2. Keeping B one point above A preserves that measured difference; the findings are real but narrower, so 3 is appropriate.

differences_remaining: design_judgment, candidate A: I keep 3 against R2's 4 because the honest 0-100% axis still yields a flat, low-information primary chart with no change view.
interaction_completeness, candidate A: I keep 4 against R2's 3 because the sampling limit is already reflected in ux_reasoning and the states/interactions themselves are implemented.
accessibility_responsiveness, candidate B: I keep 3 against R2's 2 because B has no meaningful page overflow and the same narrow axe finding set, unlike A's 580px mobile document.
summary: All three disputed positions were maintained: no counterpart evidence changed the underlying facts, only how the same facts are weighted. Candidate B remains the stronger working investigation surface and keeps the higher final total.
